questions.q: What is Bicep's `param` keyword the equivalent of, from Lesson 7?
options: Terraform's `variable "x" {}` block — a value supplied at deployment time, not hardcoded
Terraform's `output` block
A value that is always computed, never supplied externally
A resource block's symbolic name
questions.explain: Both `param` and Terraform's `variable` block exist to supply a value at deployment/apply time instead of hardcoding it.

questions.q: Why does `storageAccountName` in this lesson's example have no default value, while `location` and `skuName` do?
options: A storage account name must be globally unique, so there's no sensible default to give it
Bicep requires at least one parameter per file to have no default
Default values are not supported for string parameters
It's an arbitrary style choice with no real reason
questions.explain: A default only makes sense when there's a reasonable value to fall back to — a globally-unique name doesn't have one.

questions.q: What does the `@allowed([...])` decorator do to a parameter?
options: Restricts the parameter to a specific list of valid values, catching an invalid one before deployment
Automatically deploys the resource with the first value in the list
Deletes any resource that doesn't match one of the allowed values
Has no actual effect on validation — it's purely documentation
questions.explain: `@allowed` limited `skuName` to exactly the replication types Azure Storage actually supports.

questions.q: What's the key difference between a `param` and a `var` in Bicep?
options: A `param` is supplied from outside the file at deployment time; a `var` is always computed inside the file
There is no real difference — they're interchangeable keywords
A `var` must always have a default value; a `param` never can
`param` is used only for numbers, `var` only for strings
questions.explain: `var storageAccountNameLower = toLower(storageAccountName)` is derived entirely from something already inside the file.

questions.q: What does VS Code's Problems pane catch, and when, according to this lesson?
options: A value that violates a decorator like `@allowed` or `@minLength`, flagged live at authoring time, before any deployment command runs
Only errors that occur after a deployment has already failed
Nothing related to Bicep — it only checks JSON files
Runtime errors that occur while Azure resources are running
questions.explain: This is the same "review before it runs" idea as Terraform's plan step, just enforced one step earlier, at write time.
